text:
Dear Adagio Maestro: I am listening in from 
California USA. Born in San Francisco, Mom and I moved to Berkeley when I was 4 years old. It was she who loved classical music 🎶🎶🎶 and kept it playing inside our home 
always. My two younger sisters and I grew
up listening to Brahms, Bethoven, Chopin,
Mozart, Vivaldi, and Pavarotti --alone and 
singing with, as one of the Three Tenors.
THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR PLAYING 
THIS HEAVENLY BEAUTIFUL MUSIC FOR 
US TODAY. I fell asleep listening to it last 
night. The calming effect this has on me,
is difficult to put into words. Very emotional.
This music is my mother's love reaching 
me across time and space. Mom had a 
massive stroke at the age of 83 and she 
passed away on September 16, 2010. 
While she was in hospital, I requested the 
Nurse to keep her favorite music station,
KPFA AND KPFB --turned on, on low, day and 
night. Hearing is the last sense to go before 
death. So my mother was wafted away to 
our heavenly Father with her favorite music 
playing for her. For the angels. I am 70 years 
old 🗝️ now.  And I am in tears. I miss her
so much it hurts. This piece playing now 
is so medicinal for me because the Cello,
Piano, and Violin 🎻 are my favorite 
instruments in the orchestra. 
My mother's entire collection of music 
was stolen from my apartment in
2025, just a year ago. Along with 
everything else I had of hers. Her ashes.
Her Navajo collection. Her manual 
Typewriter. Her walker.  None of it can
ever be replaced. Thank you for bringing 
her back , even for a moment. This is her
way of summoning me. I am in constant pain and very tired. My two little sweethearts,
my therapy dogs, are also old, one is 16, 
the other is 13. Once they're gone, I, too, 
will be going home. Please keep the 
Music 🎵🎶 playing for me. 
Sincerely, Roberta Puentes 
In California USA.
